note: Where each movement stands on today’s dividing questions.

groups.era: 20th c. (roots in Ibn Taymiyya and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb)
texts: كتاب التوحيد لمحمد بن عبد الوهاب
Works of al-Albānī and Ibn ʿUthaymīn
groups.self: Returning to Islam as the Salaf practised it: pure tawḥīd, Sunna, no innovation.
beliefs: Tawḥīd in worship is the first call.
Follow the evidence over a school.

madhhab: Follow the evidence; a school is a study aid, not binding (many Saudi scholars Ḥanbalī in practice).
tasawwuf: Sufi orders rejected as innovation; purification by the Sunna accepted.
tawassul: Only by Allah’s names, one’s good deeds or a living person’s prayer; mawlid and seeking blessing at graves rejected.
politics: Obedience to Muslim rulers; no parties, protests or public criticism.
others: Other groups corrected on specific points; Muslims, not disbelievers.

groups.origin: Safar al-Ḥawālī, Salmān al-ʿAwda; influenced by Brotherhood organising
texts: Lectures and books of the Ṣaḥwa shaykhs
groups.self: Salafī belief joined to public engagement with the affairs of the Muslims.
beliefs: Rulers may be publicly advised and criticised.

tasawwuf: Sufi orders rejected as innovation; purification by the Sunna accepted.
tawassul: Only by Allah’s names, one’s good deeds or a living person’s prayer; mawlid and seeking blessing at graves rejected.

groups.origin: Abū Muḥammad al-Maqdisī, al-Qaeda; ISIS as its extreme
groups.self: Reviving jihad against rulers who do not rule by the Sharīʿa and against foreign powers.
beliefs: Loyalty and disavowal (الولاء والبراء) as a core of creed.
groups.note: Rejected and condemned by the great majority of scholars of every school, including the scholarly Salafīs, for its takfīr and violence.

creed: Atharī, with stress on ḥākimiyya and al-walāʾ wa al-barāʾ.
tasawwuf: Sufi orders rejected as innovation; purification by the Sunna accepted.
tawassul: Only by Allah’s names, one’s good deeds or a living person’s prayer; mawlid and seeking blessing at graves rejected.
politics: Current states and rulers illegitimate; revolt.
others: Takfīr of rulers and their supporters; ISIS of wide circles of Muslims.

groups.origin: Dār al-ʿUlūm Deoband; Qāsim Nānotwī, Rashīd Aḥmad Gangohī
groups.self: Ahl al-Sunna: Ḥanafī in law, Māturīdī in creed, Sufi in the path, guarding the Sunna against customs.

tasawwuf: Accepted, with practices seen as innovation removed.
tawassul: Tawassul through the Prophet ﷺ and the righteous accepted (المهند); fixed mawlid gatherings and ʿurs rejected.
politics: Varied: JUI is a party; the Tablīghī offshoot avoids politics.
arms: Mainstream against; the Taliban came out of Deobandī madrasas.
others: Critical of Barelwī practices and of anti-madhhab groups.

groups.self: Ahl al-Sunna wa al-Jamāʿa: love and honour of the Prophet ﷺ at the centre.
beliefs: The Prophet ﷺ is light (نور), given knowledge of the unseen by Allah, present and witnessing (حاضر وناظر).
Tawassul, mawlid and visiting saints’ shrines are Sunna-rooted.

tasawwuf: Central, especially Qādirī; shrines and ʿurs.
tawassul: Tawassul, mawlid and shrine visits accepted and practised.
change: Love of the Prophet ﷺ, devotional gatherings.
others: Critical of Deobandīs and Wahhābīs (a historic fatwa over certain statements).

groups.origin: Nadhīr Ḥusayn Dehlawī, Ṣiddīq Ḥasan Khān
groups.self: Following the Qur’an and ḥadīth directly, without imitation of a school.
beliefs: Practice by the authentic ḥadīth (e.g. raising hands in prayer).

tasawwuf: Sufi orders rejected as innovation; purification by the Sunna accepted.
tawassul: Only by Allah’s names, one’s good deeds or a living person’s prayer; mawlid and seeking blessing at graves rejected.

groups.origin: Ḥasan al-Bannā, Egypt; later Sayyid Quṭb, Yūsuf al-Qaraḍāwī
groups.where: Egypt, the Arab world, worldwide branches
groups.self: “A Salafī call, a Sunnī way, a Sufi reality, a political body…”: Islam as a complete way of life.
beliefs: Gradual reform from the individual up to the state.
Cooperate on what is agreed; excuse each other on the rest.

creed: Broad: Ashʿarī, Māturīdī and Atharī members.
tasawwuf: Accepted in a reformed, practical form.
tawassul: A disputed side issue, not a matter of creed (الأصول العشرون).
arms: Officially rejected since the 1970s; Quṭb’s ideas debated.

groups.self: An Islamic movement for establishing the religion (إقامة الدين) in every sphere.
beliefs: A disciplined, educated party to reform state and society.

creed: Broadly Sunnī, not tied to one kalām school.
change: A disciplined party working through ideas and elections.

groups.where: Worldwide; largest gathering at Raiwind and Tongi
groups.self: Reviving faith and practice in ordinary Muslims through going out (الخروج) in Allah’s path.
beliefs: Six points: kalima, prayer, knowledge and dhikr, honour of Muslims, sincerity, dawah.
Stay out of politics and disputes.

groups.where: Worldwide; Central Asia, the Arab world, Europe
groups.self: A political party whose aim is resuming Islamic life by re-establishing the caliphate.
beliefs: The caliphate is the first obligation of the age.
Single-chain ḥadīth not used in creed.
The party adopts specific rulings for members.

creed: Kalām-leaning; single-chain reports not accepted in creed.
politics: Work only for the caliphate; no part in non-Islamic systems.
change: Intellectual and political struggle, then seeking support from people of power (طلب النصرة).
others: Muslims are Muslims; the systems are un-Islamic.

groups.origin: Jamāl al-Dīn al-Afghānī, Muḥammad ʿAbduh, Sayyid Aḥmad Khān; later Fazlur Rahman
groups.self: Renewing Islamic thought by reason and fresh ijtihād to meet the modern age.

groups.origin: Ghulām Aḥmad Parwez, Aḥmad Ṣubḥī Manṣūr
groups.where: Small circles: South Asia, Egypt, online
texts: Works of Parwez and Ṣubḥī Manṣūr
groups.self: The Qur’an alone is the source of religion.
groups.note: Rejecting the Sunna’s authority is held by scholars of every school above to put one outside Sunnī and Shīʿī Islam.

others: Critical of ḥadīth-based Islam as a whole.
